name: Select
purpose: Lets users choose a single value from a predefined list.
neverUseFor: Free-form text entry - use Input instead
Multiple simultaneous selections - use MultiSelect or CheckboxGroup
Large option catalogs with search - use Combobox
rationale: Select is a select-only combobox on a <button> plus the Menu listbox (ADR-013) instead of a native <select>, so the popup can be styled with tokens. It has one fixed 32px height (semantic.size.m) on purpose, so the trigger and its 32px Menu rows read as one aligned scale.

mayExtendLocally: Provide the options, label, placeholder and helper text
Control the value and validation from product logic
mustEscalateToDS: Adding a size prop or new heights

authored.name: required
authored.description: The field must have a value before form submission.
authored.aria: aria-required='true'. Not natively enforced — see ADR-013's consequences; a hand-rolled trigger has no native constraint validation to inherit.

anatomy.description: Layout wrapper for label, field, and messages.

Accessible label. Always rendered - visible or sr-only. Sits exactly 8px above the trigger — see .ai/maps/patterns/form-field-spacing.md. Disabled: dims to text.disabled with the rest of the text (.ai/maps/patterns/disabled-state.md).

The required indicator (*) inside the label, the label color, 2px (spacing/3xs) after the text — shown by `required`. Disabled: dims to text.disabled with the rest of the text (.ai/maps/patterns/disabled-state.md).
Positions the trigger button and chevron.

The visible control. Real DOM focus stays here at all times — see ADR-013. `role` is implicit (button); `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` wire it to the portaled Menu.

Wraps the trigger's own displayed text (selected option's label, or placeholder). Truncates with an ellipsis at a fixed/narrow consumer-set width instead of overflowing or forcing the trigger to grow — matches a native <select>'s own behavior.

Trailing chevron icon. Flips via `aria-expanded` on the trigger, same scaleY treatment as Accordion's chevron (.ai/maps/patterns/expand-collapse-chevron.md) — now real, not the earlier documented exception, since the trigger's own React state knows whether it's open.
Helper text below the field. Sits exactly 8px below it — see .ai/maps/patterns/form-field-spacing.md. Disabled: dims to text.disabled with the rest of the text (.ai/maps/patterns/disabled-state.md).

props.name: label
props.description: Visible or screen-reader-only label. Required for a11y.

props.name: options
props.description: List of options and grouped options. Each option: { value, label, labelEnd?, disabled? } — labelEnd is short secondary text (a value, count or percentage) shown at the end of the option in the list; the trigger shows only the label.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder option shown before a selection.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text shown below the field.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks field as required. Enforced natively: an invisible form input carries the value, so an empty required Select blocks form submit exactly like a native <select> (the browser's validation message points at the field and focus lands on the trigger).

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hides the label visually but keeps it accessible.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional className for the root. Use it to set a min-width so the trigger doesn't visibly resize when a shorter/longer option is selected — Select has no built-in minimum, per CLAUDE.md's min-width/max-width policy (a consumer/pattern decision, not a system token).

height.note: One fixed size only, deliberately — no size prop. Matches semantic.size.m, the same height Input/Textarea's own 'm' field uses, so a Select trigger and its Menu items read as one continuous, aligned scale (see ADR-013's amendment).

modes.hug: Width shrinks to the control's content or container constraints.
modes.fixed: Explicit width set by the consumer.

width.note: The trigger has no minimum width — it can be as narrow as its content. The minimum width rule lives on the popup (Menu contract, sizing.width): 150px for word options, none for numeric-only lists.

a11y.role: combobox on the <button> trigger (WAI-ARIA select-only combobox) + hand-rolled listbox popup (Menu) — see ADR-013. Not a native <select>.
keyboardNav: Arrow Up/Down - opens the menu, or moves the highlighted option while open
Home/End - jump to first/last enabled option while open
Enter/Space - open the menu, or confirm the highlighted option while open
Escape - close without changing the selection
Tab - move focus (closes the menu first)

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

properties.name: state
properties.description: Figma-only axis: hover/focus are CSS pseudo-classes,  open is the listbox showing (aria-expanded). invalid,  disabled and the secondary toggles are their own variants (contracts/figma-conversion.json,  pattern form-field).

options.reason: the options are drawn by the nested Menu, not by the Select: state=open holds an exposed Menu instance and the designer picks how many options it lists on that Menu (its own options = 2 … 7 VARIANT) — the Select itself has no options property (owner's decision 2026-10-21)

value.reason: the trigger shows either the placeholder (empty) or the chosen option (selected) in one text layer,   which Figma can bind to one text property only — so value picks the look and valueText is the chosen label; selected is drawn once (owner-approved option A)

figma.structure: select-root (8px gap) > select-label (text + select-required),  select-wrapper > select-trigger (hugs its text like code: select-trigger-label + select-chevron; open uses an unrotated ChevronUp,  code flips the chevron),  select-description,  select-error. state=open holds the listbox as a nested Menu instance named menu (multiple=false,  options=5,  exposed so its options 2–7 are picked from the Select's panel): absolute,  4px below select-trigger at its width,  150px minimum,  like Menu.tsx; its MenuItems read Designer,  Engineer,  Product Manager,  Tech Lead,  Other (Storybook Default),  none selected.
figma.variantCombinations: 40 variants (2026-10-21): invalid × state default/hover/focus/open = 8,  disabled = 1,  value=selected once (default,  valid,  enabled) = 1 — each of those 10 drawn with fullWidth (320px) × hideLabel false/true = 40 (variants.secondary,  owner's decision 2026-10-21). The option count is the nested Menu's options property,  not a Select variant. value=empty binds the trigger label to placeholder,  value=selected to valueText.
